operatorApprovalContractDesign.kind: Future trusted operator attestation of a NEW explicit user approval; utility validates but NEVER creates/invents the approval.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.approvalId: fresh32hex; O_EXCL claim, never reused even after aborted mint
operatorApprovalContractDesign.referenceRule: New safe immutable approval-attestation reference/path + exact SHA; cannot reuse the first or blocked second capture user approval. Local user-attestation bytes are not cryptographic proof of conversation authenticity.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.freshness: Finite numeric times, no bool, not future, unexpired, maximum window900s; authorization expiry cannot exceed this explicit approval expiry.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.credentialIdentitySource: Read only previously approved non-secret identity evidence or exact legacy authorization to extract its identity digest with provenance. Reconstruct target from fixed profile, never copy old authorization as new template. Actual credential bytes only checked by future formal runner. If no independently bound digest exists, STOP; do not read credentials to manufacture it.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.noOldApprovalReuse: Old per-attempt approval reference/ID is historical only. /2 userApprovalRef remains the fixed SOURCE proposal reference; unique fresh USER approval is separately bound by READY+consume receipts. These two concepts must not be conflated.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.absentFileCase: Only explicit expectedCanonicalState=ABSENT and no unfinished lifecycle records permits initial mint.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.referenceUniqueness: Reserve both approvalId and approvalReferenceSha256 in separate immutable claim namespaces; changing ID cannot reuse the same user approval evidence. Cryptographic binding is to the attestation bytes, not a claim of automatic chat authenticity verification.
operatorApprovalContractDesign.credentialProvenancePathPolicy: The evidence path is only a checked reference to a source-proposal-authorized safe evidence artifact or the exact current/archived old authorization; never an arbitrary readable path and never connectionDirectory. Reject any provenance outside that finite allowlist.

concurrency.selected: persistent per-plan fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) + O_EXCL durable claims
concurrency.lockLifetime: Mint holds lock for all validation/archive/stage/publication; runner holds same lock from canonical read until rollback, receipt write, consumed archival and outcome finalization.
concurrency.lockFile: 0600 owner-only regular nlink1 O_NOFOLLOW O_CLOEXEC; created exclusively when absent, otherwise validated; never unlink/recreate lock inode. Validate fd identity against directory entry before action.
concurrency.failure: LOCK_BUSY stops immediately; no waiting loop, PID timeout takeover or automatic retry.
concurrency.flockLimitation: Advisory cooperating-process serialization, not defense against root or an operator editing files outside protocol. Trusted OS-operator boundary retained.
concurrency.durableClaims: ApprovalId, explicit USER approvalReferenceSha256 and new nonceSha256 each get separate permanent O_EXCL claims before publication; source proposal raw SHA is NOT used as the per-attempt approval reference. Every partial/malformed existing claim burns that identity and blocks reuse. The auth raw SHA consume claim is durable before credentials.
concurrency.O_EXCLOnlyAlternative: Can serialize but stale crash lock requires a new recovery protocol; use flock for live lock and durable phase state for crash stop.
concurrency.privateDirectoryOnlyAlternative: 0700 protects ownership but does not serialize two same-UID operators.
concurrency.FDInheritance: Lock fd close-on-exec; inherited DB children must not prolong lock. Parent crash still leaves consume/incomplete phase records denying replay/new mint.

atomicity.primitive: Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE), via stdlib ctypes existing libc symbol; no new package/image
atomicity.sameFilesystem: Archive, pending and canonical all under fixed authorizationDirectory; validate device and mount/path identity. Receipt root can be separately synced; final READY gate coordinates rather than claiming cross-filesystem atomic transaction.
atomicity.noReplace: Collision including symlink/directory or same-hash archive path is failure; no overwrite, dedup shortcut, link/unlink workaround or copy+replace.
atomicity.durability: fsync new file plus relevant parent directories; after move fsync source+destination directories. READY is immutable and hash-bound. Runner revalidates/durably confirms readiness before writing consumed claim.
atomicity.pathSafety: Validate every existing parent, dirfd with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, regular0600 nlink1 file, owner/currentUID; fixed basenames only; compare lstat/fstat identities before/after moves. No automatic chmod/chown/repair.
atomicity.supportEvidence: Read-only check: Linux, glibc2.43, libc renameat2 symbol present. No rename or filesystem capability test performed in A1. Future owned tests must prove actual filesystem support; ENOSYS/EINVAL/EXDEV or fsync errors STOP with no weaker fallback.
atomicity.archiveBeforeReceiptCrash: PREPARED includes exact old hash and destination; after crash either old canonical or archive remains, never old-byte deletion. Ambiguous/missing combinations halt.
atomicity.recovery: No automated restart-resume/rollback/fallback command in initial utility. New implementation must detect unresolved operations and STOP; separate later exact recovery approval can append resolution evidence, never erase claim or reactivate old auth.
atomicity.directoryCreation: Create missing approved private runtime directories individually with mode0700; validate every already-existing parent rather than parents=True mode assumptions. Do not fix existing directory modes or mutate umask. An unexpected parent mode/owner or wrong mount is a hard failure.

mintStateMachine.action: Validate exact fixed paths and parent identities/modes, acquire persistent per-plan flock; load fresh operator approval and source proposal; validate source/plan/migration/risk/loss/F2/stage; refuse unexpired active auth or unresolved prior operation. No credential or DB access.

Generate new rotationId and fresh nonce; create exclusive operation directory and PREPARED receipt; reserve approvalId, explicit user approvalReferenceSha256 and new nonce hash in separate durable O_EXCL namespaces. Partial/malformed claims count as burned/unresolved. Bootstrap also permanently reserves the known old nonce hash as HISTORICAL_USED, explicitly bound to old raw SHA and first-capture evidence, before moving that old file. A historical reservation collision is failure, not silent reuse. All future minted nonces already have permanent reservations.

If expected old exists: exact SHA, type/mode/owner/nlink, expiry or terminal-consumed status and historical linkage all match. renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) canonical to SHA-addressed same-filesystem archive. Never rm/truncate/edit/copy; fsync both directory FDs, verify archived SHA/inode/content, write ARCHIVED receipt. For bootstrap old /2, use exact historical SHA/structure instead of current expiry/package validator; never authorize its execution.

Build /2 from current fixed authorities, new timestamps and nonce, safe credential identity provenance. Use private O_EXCL pending file, fsync file+directory, verify0600/UID/nlink1, exact schema and authorize_capture. Persist STAGED record with raw/canonical hashes. Recheck time/stage/source before publish; never extend expiry.

Require canonical absent; renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) pending to canonical within authorization filesystem; no overwrite/os.replace fallback. fsync affected directories and verify exact canonical SHA/identity, write PUBLISHED phase. Runner cannot dispatch yet.

Write final capture-authorization-rotation/1 READY receipt keyed by new raw SHA, binding all phases, archive, approval, source and auth identities. File+directory fsync complete before utility reports MINTED_READY. This is sole mint commit record; no later obligatory second commit file. Missing/partial/invalid READY means blocked even if canonical exists. READY validation must verify the approval-ID claim, approval-reference claim, new nonce claim and (for legacy bootstrap) the historical nonce claim and their exact rotation/authorization bindings.

crashWindows.durableState: Exactly one complete published auth and final valid READY exist.
crashWindows.failClosed: Mint is committed; no duplicate mint or replay. Only a later separately invoked runner may consume that one fresh approval. Utility never dispatches.

crashWindows.durableState: Consumed claim exists, even if malformed; DB may never have been opened.
crashWindows.failClosed: Authorization burned, second runner denied. No claim deletion/retry; state described as local dispatch claimed, not DB activity proven.

crashWindows.durableState: Consumed claim durable, canonical may remain; baseline may or may not be durable.
crashWindows.failClosed: Same authorization cannot replay; unresolved outcome prevents new lifecycle mint. Preserve UNKNOWN/NOT_PERSISTED as appropriate; no recovery of memory or control-flow-only success.

publicDocumentation.title: Linux rename(2)
publicDocumentation.claim: RENAME_NOREPLACE rejects an existing destination; filesystem support required; cross-mount rename can fail EXDEV.
publicDocumentation.inference: Use same authorization tree and fail on unsupported operation; do not use overwrite rename as fallback.

publicDocumentation.title: Linux flock(2)
publicDocumentation.claim: Advisory lock on open file description, nonblocking LOCK_NB available; locks released when all associated descriptors close.
publicDocumentation.inference: Shared stable lock inode must never be unlinked; durable journals needed beyond process death.

publicDocumentation.title: Linux fsync(2)
publicDocumentation.claim: File fsync alone does not necessarily flush parent directory entry; directory fsync is required.
publicDocumentation.inference: Durably sync both move parents and final READY/consume records.

limitations: Owner-only hash-bound local evidence is not cryptographically tamper-proof against root/same-UID operator outside protocol.
Linux rename/fsync/fsystem support requires future owned validation; A1 checked symbol presence only.
No fresh credential identity proof during lifecycle: only prior safe identity attestation; formal runner verifies actual credentials before connection.
Initial implementation has no automatic recovery/cleanup; incomplete journals require separate exact review.
